conceptTag: The first 100 days of an app
readerTitle: Forty shops signed up. Six came back. Now what?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (동네 가게용 재고 주문 앱, 지역 도매상) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 앱의 첫 100일에는 가입자를 늘리기보다 손으로 직접 도와 문제를 찾고, 고객이 실제로 가치를 얻는지 보여주는 숫자 하나로 판단한다.
misconception: 앱은 출시 후 광고와 기능 추가로 가입자를 늘리면 자란다. 다운로드 수가 늘면 잘되고 있는 것이다.

sources.text: PIXO 유닛 개념 레슨 ENT-05-01 (확장되지 않는 일 하기), ENT-05-02 (숫자 하나에 집중하기)
모든 수치와 사례는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 수치가 서로 맞는지 확인하세요: 1주차 가입 40곳, 10일차 재주문 6곳, 90일차 가입 약 60곳 중 매주 주문 34곳. 차트 값은 6 → 9 → 17 → 26 → 34입니다.
이 레슨은 적용 레슨이므로 새 개념을 소개하지 않습니다. 정리 카드에 사용한 개념 두 개(ENT-05-01, ENT-05-02)를 명시했습니다. 주스 바 적용 레슨(ENT-05-07)과 장면이나 선택지가 겹치지 않는지 확인하세요.

cards.title: Forty shops signed up. Six came back.
body: Two founders launch an app that lets corner shops reorder stock from a local wholesaler in a few taps.
In the first week, 40 shop owners download it. By day 10, only six have placed a second order. The next 90 days decide whether this becomes a business.

image.label: A phone with an ordering app on a corner shop counter
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 동네 가게 계산대 위에 주문 앱이 켜진 휴대폰, 옆에 손글씨 메모가 적힌 종이 공책. 화면 위에 "40 signed up / 6 came back" 말풍선. 실제 브랜드 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: People sign up, then stop. What do you do first?
body: You have savings for about a year and no staff. The app works without bugs. Shop owners just don't come back.

options.text: Run ads to sign up 200 more shops
options.feedback: More signups pour into the same leaky bucket. You'd pay to learn the same lesson, with less money left.

options.text: Spend two weeks in the shops, placing orders next to the owners
options.feedback: This is **doing things that don't scale**. It's slow and can't last, but it shows you where the app fails in a real shop.

options.text: Email all 40 owners a survey about what to improve
options.feedback: Cheap and quick, but busy owners rarely reply, and what they write may differ from what they do at the counter.

cards.title: The rival wasn't another app. It was a notebook.
body: Sitting by the till, the founders saw the real problem. Owners didn't reorder during the day. They checked shelves after closing, tired, with a paper notebook.
The app asked for a login and a product search. The notebook asked for nothing.
So for three weeks, the founders photographed notebook pages and typed the orders in themselves. Then they built one feature that copied the habit: **snap a photo of your list, confirm the order**.

image.label: A notebook order list turning into an app order
image.brief: 왼쪽에 손글씨 재고 목록이 적힌 공책, 가운데 휴대폰으로 사진을 찍는 손, 오른쪽에 정리된 주문 화면. 화살표로 세 단계 연결. 따뜻한 저녁 가게 조명. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: Which number do you watch?
body: The dashboard now shows downloads, signups, total orders, money ordered, and shops that order every week. You can only push hard on one.

options.feedback: Easy to grow and nice to share with investors, but it says nothing about whether shops keep using the app.

options.text: Shops that place an order every week
options.feedback: This is **focusing on one number**. A shop that reorders weekly is getting real help. Grow that, and most other numbers follow.
It matters for revenue, but one big shop can lift it while most others quietly drift away.

cards.title: The number starts moving.
body: After the photo feature, the weekly ordering number grew steadily. Signups grew far less, to about 60 shops by day 90. The founders kept visiting a few new shops each week.

cards.title: Hand work and one number both have limits.
body: Typing orders by hand teaches you fast, but it hides a cost. Before you count a shop as won, ask whether it would stay if you stopped helping.
A single number can also mislead. Chase weekly orders too hard and you might nudge owners into tiny orders they don't need. Check it against something real, like order size.
And the right number changes as you grow. Later it may be profit per shop.

cards.title: A wholesaler offers you 500 shops.
body: A regional wholesaler likes the app. It offers to tell all 500 of its shop customers to use it next month, if you add its price list.
Your team is still the two of you.

options.text: Accept and launch for all 500 next month
options.feedback: A huge jump in signups, but you can't visit 500 shops. If most stall like your first 40, your weekly number falls and the wholesaler loses faith.

options.text: Start with 30 of its shops, set them up by hand, and judge by weekly orders
options.feedback: You keep the **unscalable help** that worked, and your **one number** tells you within weeks whether to widen the deal.
You keep your focus, but you skip a channel full of the right customers. Testing it small costs little.

cards.title: In the first 100 days, learn by hand and measure one thing.
body: This lesson used two ideas from the unit. **Do things that don't scale** found the real problem on day 10 and shaped the day 80 deal. **Focus on one number** kept the founders from chasing downloads on day 40.
**Try it today:** write down the one number that shows your customers getting value. Then pick one task you'd normally automate and do it by hand this week.
